messages.content: "Could you first fetch the top 10 popular artworks at the Metropolitan Museum of Art sorted by popularity and then fetch the top 5 artworks sorted chronologically? After that, could you search for ongoing lawsuits related to Google that were filed in California starting from January 1, 2020? Lastly, could you also find any settled lawsuits related to Microsoft that were filed in New York starting from January 1, 2018?"

function.name: metropolitan_museum_get_top_artworks
function.description: Fetches the list of popular artworks at the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Results can be sorted based on popularity. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

number.description: The number of artworks to fetch

sort_by.description: The criteria to sort the results on. Default is 'popularity'.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a specific company within a specific date range and location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

company.description: The company related to the lawsuit.

start_date.description: Start of the date range for when the lawsuit was filed.

location.description: Location where the lawsuit was filed.

status.description: The status of the lawsuit. Default is 'ongoing'.

We should do them sequentially. According to policy, we can only make one function call per assistant turn. But we can chain calls? We need separate turns. But we can do multiple turns. The user asked for four tasks. We can do them in order: first call for top 10 sorted by popularity; second call for top 5 sorted chronologically; third call for lawsuits for Google; fourth call for settled lawsuits for Microsoft.

We need to produce four function calls. Each call must be separate. We'll output them one after another. The system will respond with results. That seems fine.

We need to use correct JSON format. For the first call: number=10, sort_by="popularity". For second: number=5, sort_by="chronological". Third: company="Google", start_date="2020-01-01", location="California", status="ongoing". Fourth: company="Microsoft", start_date="2018-01-01", location="New York", status="settled".

We'll produce four calls.
